status.en: 139 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Balochistan.
status.nb: 139 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Belutsjistan.

summary.en: Pakistani security forces continue to face cross-border attacks, with recent landmine blasts killing four men near the LoC in Azad Kashmir and another four Pakistani infiltrators killed in a blast in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district. Afghan Taliban fighters are accused of using Afghan soil to launch attacks into Pakistan, prompting Pakistan to urge the Taliban to stop such cross-border militant activity. A blasphemy allegation sparked an attack on a Christian family’s home and clinic in Pakistan, while the Taliban are exploiting European anti-migrant sentiment. The conflict remains deadly, with 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker fortsetter å møte grenseoverskridende angrep, med nylige landmineeksplosjoner som drepte fire menn nær LoC i Azad Kashmir og ytterligere fire pakistanske infiltranter drept i en eksplosjon i Jammu og Kasmirs Poonch-distrikt. Afghanske Taliban-krigere blir anklaget for å bruke afghansk jord til å lansere angrep inn i Pakistan, noe som får Pakistan til å oppfordre Taliban til å stoppe slik grenseoverskridende militantaktivitet. En blasfemianklage utløste et angrep på en kristen families hjem og klinikk i Pakistan, mens Taliban utnytter europeisk anti-migrasjonsstemning. Konflikten forblir dødelig, med 1 794 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
